task_specification.objective: Harden dense-profile receipt qualification for native host recapture while delivering a regression-safe release pass that preserves authored upgrade-choice hierarchy and arena spatial integrity.

diagnosis.root_cause: Dense-profile candidate instrumentation exists, but native qualification remains dependent on an external renderer/collector and lacks a fully deterministic candidate-to-host receipt handoff. The same release pass must also preserve the required player-facing choice visual hierarchy and arena spatial integrity while making that handoff recapturable.

stop_conditions: Do not qualify software/llvmpipe output as native performance evidence.
Do not replace or surgically alter the authored CemeteryGarden package or preserved gameplay assets.
Do not change ordinary-run defaults or expose tester controls in release exports.
Do not replay ambiguous stateful collector actions; GameLoop Runtime owns rebind and recapture, and Tester owns verdict.
If existing choice or arena behavior already satisfies the acceptance predicates, preserve it and make only directly necessary integration fixes.

strategy.rationale: Use explicit isolation and contract auditing rather than another round of dense tuning: make phase, cycle, timeout, renderer, and reset receipts self-validating, then perform a same-pass black-box regression guard over the mandated choice and arena surfaces.

code: Run Godot/GDScript parse and project checks on all targeted scripts/scenes.
Exercise dense self-audit fixtures for valid, duplicate, incomplete, software-renderer, timeout, and reset-isolation-failure cases; verify deterministic bounded receipts.
Verify ordinary-run and release guards leave tester controls inert and preserve lifecycle reset behavior.

Run focused UI/state checks confirming silhouettes or icons, truthful current-to-new values, at most three decision-relevant deltas, and keyboard/mouse/gamepad focus states; run focused spatial checks for expanded/larger traversable scale, external depth, landmark collision, boundary visibility, and ordinary movement replay.
runtime: GameLoop Runtime rebinds the candidate-scoped collector when available and runs one fresh serial tester_dense_prepare → tester_dense_advance → tester_dense_reset sequence per cycle for three native 1920x1080 cycles with nonzero distributions.

Runtime verifies no stale sampling, runaway active-enemy growth, leaked pooled nodes, runtime error spam, or reset contamination, then reruns validate:release_convergence_dense_run_performance_contract.
Tester recaptures choice-draft focus states and arena spawn, landmark, perimeter, and ordinary-movement views; Tester retains closure authority.
Preservation checks rerun validate:native_godot_project and validate:host_godot_boot.
visual: Capture sparse shipped-gameplay dense start/peak/reset views plus upgrade-draft focused and unfocused states and arena spawn/landmark/perimeter views.

Confirm authored CemeteryGarden composition, HUD readability, silhouettes/icons, current-to-new comparison, landmark collision visibility, and external depth remain stable; visual evidence does not replace the native performance verdict.

done_when: A release-guarded dense self-audit reports immutable contract signature/version, 25-40 enemy range, target density, 1920x1080 requirement, required metric names, three-cycle requirement, and prepare/advance/reset ordering.

Each dense cycle emits unique cycle identity plus requested, resolved, reset_isolation, setup_generation, and advance_generation receipts; incomplete, stale, duplicate, or timeout states resolve to bounded pending/rejected receipts instead of ambiguous sampling.

The aggregate snapshot includes nonzero-capable frame, physics, render, allocation, subsystem, active/pooled entity, lifecycle-delta, and runtime-error distributions with bounded history and no per-frame log spam.
Native qualification is true only after three distinct complete native cycles with nonzero samples and reset isolation; software and unknown renderers remain explicitly rejected or pending.

Upgrade choices retain a clear choice visual hierarchy led by authored silhouettes or icons, compact truthful current-to-new values, no more than three decision-relevant stat deltas, no unchanged or placeholder CURRENT rows, restrained copy, and complete keyboard, mouse, and gamepad focus states.

The arena provides larger traversable scale or an equivalent expand behavior, a coherent external world/external depth, a visible central building or landmark, aligned collision, and stable visibility without disappearance or occlusion drift at the boundary/perimeter during ordinary movement or movement replay.

Host can run tester_dense_prepare, tester_dense_advance, and tester_dense_reset serially for three isolated native cycles and evaluate release_convergence_dense_run_performance_contract without replaying an outcome-unknown advance; ordinary gameplay and native boot remain unchanged.
tasks.instructions: Inspect the existing dense_profile.gd and RunController control flow, then add only missing contract-level receipt/audit behavior. Preserve current pooling, lifecycle counters, sampling, renderer gate, authored map bindings, and ordinary defaults. Validate phase transitions, cycle identity uniqueness, required metric/distribution presence, bounded sample history, timeout closure, and reset isolation; expose a compact machine-readable receipt through the existing dense snapshot path and document the one-shot host sequence. Keep tester actions editor-only and release-disabled, and preserve deferred renderer-gate ordering so software diagnostics are collected before explicit native rejection. In the same bounded pass, verify and directly repair only regressions in the player-facing choice visual hierarchy (silhouettes/icons, truthful current-to-new values, no more than three decision-relevant stat deltas, keyboard/mouse/gamepad focus) and arena spatial integrity (expand or larger traversable scale, external world or external depth, central building or landmark, collision, no disappearance or occlusion, boundary or perimeter, ordinary movement or movement replay). Do not fabricate native samples or claim phase closure; external collector rebind and formal recapture remain host-owned.
